facts: Darrin Davis and Chief Montez put the badge on the pickleball court. First Youth Community Event is the Badge & Paddle Classic

The Darrin Davis Community Youth Events program announced its first event this cycle: the Badge & Paddle Pickleball Classic, a free doubles tournament in East Oakland that puts Oakland kids, neighborhood residents and OPD officers on the same court. Partners are drawn at random, so nobody plays with who they came with. A teenager from Deep East might get a beat officer, a grandmother from Fruitvale might get the Chief. Davis announced it alongside Chief Rafael Montez, and the pairing is the point. The two met three years ago through the A's community policing work, with ride-alongs, youth clinics and school visits in West Oakland and Fruitvale, and what started as PR became a real friendship. Davis majored in criminal justice at Ohio State, was made an honorary police captain in his hometown of Columbus in 2032, and keeps that badge in his locker next to his batting gloves. His line has always been "Baseball's what I do. Justice is what I believe." Davis framed the tournament as the opposite of a crisis response: a chance for people to meet officers on a Saturday when nothing is wrong, and for officers to meet the neighborhoods they patrol by first name. Responders from the Oakland Alternative Response Initiative have been invited to enter a team, putting OPD and the behavioral health crews on the same bracket. OPD is the program's sponsor with support from the A's and Oaks, and every event stays free. Open questions: does Montez actually play, which A's and Oaks players sign up, and does Davis keep the program going if his playing days are winding down at 32 after missing major time twice in three seasons?
